about: The application engine's process. Nodes come from what a finished application must CONTAIN, not from a list of past mistakes. Each node names the check that decides whether it is done. The last node is 'ready': the engine never submits and never sends.

nodes.label: Capture the posting verbatim
rules: Save the posting VERBATIM to jd-posting.txt, plus listing metadata that is not in the body: compensation, location, hiring region, visa or relocation lines, the apply-to route.
Read the BODY for a country or work-authorization line. A job board's structured field can say 'anywhere' while the body says otherwise. The body wins.
Write jd-analysis.md in the same step: requirements marked MET / PARTIAL / GAP against the career bank.

nodes.label: List what the POSTING demands an application include
rules: Write required-artifacts.json: {"read_by": "<who read the posting for this>", "items": [...]}. Each item names an artifact (cover letter, portfolio link, a specific question, a work sample) and optionally the channel it belongs to.
Postings bury hard requirements in the last paragraph ('applications without a cover letter will not be considered'). Read to the end.
An empty list is a valid answer, but it must be an explicit empty list, not a missing file.

nodes.label: Proceed or skip, with every bar quoted
rules: Write eligibility.md ending in 'VERDICT: PROCEED' or 'VERDICT: SKIP', and a 'COMPENSATION:' line of CLEARS, BELOW or UNKNOWN taken from resume-data/salary-thresholds.md. Never guess a figure.
Reject only on a factual bar: a stated country or work-authorization requirement, a capability the career bank's ceilings rule out, or pay below the walk-away threshold.
Years of experience is never a bar on its own. Timezone and working hours are never a bar.
Every rejection quotes the posting line that caused it. A rejection with no quote is an assumption.
On SKIP, end the run with 'apply.py abort' and record the reason in resume-data/job-search/. A skipped application is a normal outcome.

nodes.label: Find every channel and decide each one
rules: Write channels.json. One entry per channel you checked (job board, the company's careers page, a published email address). Status is INTENDED, NOT_AVAILABLE or DEFERRED, and every entry says what was checked in 'evidence'.
A channel you did not pursue is NOT_AVAILABLE with what you looked at, or DEFERRED with a reason. A blank entry fails: silence is how single-channel applications happen by accident.

Each INTENDED channel lists in 'contains': 'answers' (paths to answer, cover letter or cover email files), 'resume', optional 'attachments', and 'posting_artifacts' (what it includes from required-artifacts.json).
Do not guess email addresses (careers@, jobs@). Use only an address the employer publishes. If none exists, the channel is NOT_AVAILABLE.

nodes.label: Question brief, argument brief and company research for every answer
rules: For each answer file answers/<id>.md: briefs/<id>-question-brief.md (question-interpreter, written blind to the career bank) and briefs/<id>-argument-brief.md (application-strategist).
The argument brief records 3-5 angles and which were REJECTED, with why. A brief with one angle means the first idea was taken.
company-research.md exists before any answer makes a claim about the employer.

nodes.label: Write every answer an intended channel needs
rules: Writing order per answer: interpreter, strategist, writer. The writer may improve the route but not the evidence boundary.
An anchor must be something that would become false if a competitor said it. A fact about the industry is not an anchor however well sourced.
Respect stated word limits. Never volunteer a weakness that was not asked about.

nodes.label: No answer reheated from another application
rules: Compares each answer against the answers of every other application folder that reached 'ready'.
Reused evidence is not automatically wrong, because your best material is finite. A shared run of six or more words means the answer itself was reused.
Change the evidence or the angle, not the wording. Rewording a reused answer keeps it reused.

nodes.label: Every claim traced; every unsupported sentence answered
rules: This RUNS the grounder over every answer. It never accepts a hand-written grounding file.
Every UNSUPPORTED sentence needs a disposition in grounding/<id>.json: "SOURCE:career-bank.md:<line>", "RHETORICAL" or "CUT" (and then actually cut it).
'In my experience' or 'what I have found' in front of a generalisation makes it sound sourced without sourcing it. Find the career-bank line or cut the claim.
A figure must appear literally in a source. Topical overlap is not support for a number.

Watch scope: a true fact about one team restated about 'the whole operation' is the most common defect. The grounder flags it when a figure or absence claim is attached; it cannot see the figureless case.
REVIEW sentences do not block, but they are listed for the verifier: weak support is where invented detail hides.

nodes.label: application-verifier passes every answer, by name
rules: The verifier reads only the final answer, the question, jd-posting.txt, company-research.md and the career bank. Never the briefs.
verification.md names each answer file in a heading ('## answers/<id>.md') and ends that section with 'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FAIL'. The LAST verdict for a file is the one that counts.
A verdict written before the answer last changed does not count: re-verify after every repair.
This node re-runs the grounder on the current text first, so a repaired answer cannot pass on an earlier grounding.

nodes.label: Tailored resume reviewed and rendered
rules: resume.md in the folder, reviewed in review.md ending 'VERDICT: READY', with the review newer than resume.md.
Render only after the review passes. A render older than resume.md is stale: re-render it.
Rendered files are checked by EXTRACTED text against resume-data/banned-terms.txt, because the PDF is what an employer reads, not the markdown.

nodes.label: Everything a reviewer needs is present and hashed
rules: A reviewer can only review what it is given: every answer, the resume, the career bank, the posting and company-research.md must exist and are hashed into evidence-pack.json.
Attach the real files to any reviewer. Never hand it a summary of the career bank.
A file that changed after it was reviewed is a new draft. The later checks compare against these hashes.

nodes.label: Optional second opinion, or a recorded decision to skip it
rules: Either review/review-round-<n>.md names each answer and the resume PDF and ends 'VERDICT: READY TO SUBMIT', or external-review-skipped.md gives a 'REASON:' line. Skipping is allowed; skipping silently is not.
A review older than the file it reviews does not count.

Apply a reviewer's fix only after checking it against the career bank. Record every rejected fix and why. A reviewer cannot see your corrections, so a fact it asks you to restore may be one you removed on purpose.

nodes.label: Composition: each channel carries answers, resume and every required artifact
rules: An application is incomplete unless the recipient can, from what they receive alone, see who is applying, read why, and get everything the posting asked for.
An email channel needs a resume in its attachments. A board or careers-page channel needs the resume it will upload recorded in 'resume'.
Evidence the argument brief banned for this application (banned-evidence.txt) must not appear in any answer or in the tailored resume.

nodes.label: Ready for you to submit
rules: Writes READY-FOR-YOU.md: per channel, what to submit, where, and which files.
THE ENGINE STOPS HERE. It never submits an application and never sends an email. Show the user the application. The user submits it.
